inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,070M shares on the FY2026 10-K cover (2026-11-02) + 9M dilutive RSU equivalents (FY2026 10-K EPS note, treasury method). Up from 1,066M at the prior build because the Modular acquisition (closed 2026-07-28, one day after the Q3 10-Q cover date) was paid in 18M new shares -- genuine non-SBC issuance, already in the count, so nothing further is projected. Held FLAT from here because SBC and equity-award withholding taxes are fully expensed in the flows (charging dilution too would double-count). QCOM is a heavy repurchaser ($7.8B FY26, $8.8B FY25), so the flat count is funded, not a convention. The September 2026 Amazon customer warrant (25M shares, strike $161.26, 10-year term, 4M vested) is NOT added: it is at/out of the money on the treasury method at the current price and its fair value ($1.8B) is charged as a reduction of revenue as it vests, so it is already inside the revenue and margin paths. The 4M Alphawave Exchangeable Shares are presented with common stock in the financial statements; if the cover count excludes them the divisor is ~0.4% light.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation expense $3,452M (operating add-back) + payments of tax withholdings related to vesting of share-based awards $1,134M (financing). QCOM publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. FY25: $2,783M + $1,115M = $3,898M (8.8% of revenue). The FY26 step-up includes a two-year equity award that replaces the FY26 and FY27 annual cash bonus for non-executive leadership.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 5.07% (10y UST, Yahoo ^TNX 2026-11-18; it has been 4.7-5.3% for three months), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.2 (fabless semi, handset-cycle exposure) -> cost of equity ~11.1%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.8% (after-tax ~4.7%) on ~8% debt weight -> WACC ~10.6%, rounded down to 10.25% for QTL's royalty stability (the same 0.3pt allowance as the prior build). CHANGED from 9.5%: the prior build's 4.3% risk-free rate was stale -- the 10-year was already ~4.9% on 2026-10-02, and QCOM's own September 2026 warrant valuation used 4.7%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclical and customer risk is carried in the scenario drivers and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial relative to EV ($1.1B future payments); kept out of both flows and net debt, consistent with US GAAP opex treatment (rent sits inside EBITDA).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing: US fabless semiconductor + patent licensing operating company; cyclical, so mid-cycle margins and a 14x cyclical cap rather than a growth-tech 20x). Same model as the 2026-10-02 build; this is an UPDATE to FY2026 actuals (10-K filed 2026-11-04). FY0 = FY2026 actual: revenue $43,120M (prior estimate $42,898M; Q4 came in at $10,322M vs the $10,100M guidance midpoint). Reported FCF $8,651M = OCF $11,145M - capex $2,494M (prior estimate $9,300M); owner FCF $4,065M (9.4% margin) after $4,586M SBC + withholding -- depressed by a $2.1B inventory build to secure supply, the final $663M repatriation-tax instalment and capex that doubled; FY25 owner FCF was $8,922M (20.1%). Year-1 component-built base owner FCF ~$4.7B (11.0%). Adj EBITDA here = GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC: FY22 44.5% (peak), FY23 33.7%, FY24 37.0%, FY25 37.8%, FY26 31.9% (32.6% before $332M restructuring), sliding through the year: Q1 37.9%, Q2 33.8%, Q3 28.7%, Q4 ~25.8% (the restructuring charge falls mostly in H2). Net debt from the FY26 balance sheet: debt $15,112M (short-term $2,492M incl. $499M CP + long-term $12,620M) less cash $4,636M and marketable securities $3,045M. Interest income NOT stripped: QCOM is net debt, and the engine builds unlevered flows from EBITDA, so neither interest income nor expense is in the projected FCF. QSI non-marketable venture stakes are excluded from the bridge (conservative). GUIDANCE GAP: QCOM guides one quarter at a time and the Q1 FY27 guidance in the 2026-11-04 earnings 8-K was not retrievable in this run (sec.gov refused the request); year 1 is judged from the 10-K 'Looking Forward' section instead (memory-supply constraints hurting handset OEM demand for 'the next several quarters', supplier cost inflation with pricing relief in H2 FY27, data-center shipments ramping from Q1 FY27 under hyperscaler custom-silicon agreements, capex to rise from FY26 levels). Replace the year-1 growth and margin with the guidance-implied figures when the release is in hand. UNCHANGED BY DECISION (and what would move them): growth from year 4 on (a second hyperscaler programme or a QTL rate challenge); mature EBITDA margins 36/38.5/32% (evidence that the H2 FY27 pricing actions do or do not restore QCT gross margin, and the gross margin of custom silicon once it is a visible share of revenue); terminal cash tax 19%; working-capital capture -10%; terminal growth and the 14/16/12x caps; scenario weights 25/50/25; bear and bull year-1 growth.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable: book value was gutted by the FY2018 $22.6B tender/recap (equity $31B -> $0.8B) and is rebuilding from that floor, and FY26 equity was lifted by the $5.7B valuation-allowance release and $4.5B of stock issued in acquisitions, so the 5y equity CAGR (25.0%) diverges >30% from revenue (5.1%) and EPS (10.0%). EPS is distorted by the FY2025 $5.7B deferred-tax charge and its FY2026 reversal (FY26 EPS $12.70 includes ~$5.40 of non-cash tax benefit). Through-cycle 10y revenue CAGR (6.2%) is the honest anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes: FY21 $6,241M, FY22 $4,007M, FY23 $6,844M, FY24 $7,581M, FY25 $8,922M, FY26 $4,065M. The owner-FCF CAGRs (-15.9% 3y, -8.2% 5y) are now well BELOW reported FCF (-4.2%, 0.0%): SBC + withholding rose from 8.8% to 10.6% of revenue in FY26 while reported FCF fell, i.e. a rising share of a shrinking cash flow is being paid in stock. FY26 is a trough year for cash conversion (inventory build, capex doubling), so the negative CAGRs overstate the trend, but the SBC direction is real.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 0% (was -1% on a lower estimated base): handsets fall again from $24.1B toward the ~$21-22B H2 FY26 run-rate as memory-supply constraints cut OEM builds, offset by automotive (FY26 $6.0B, +52%, Q4 annualising ~$8B), IoT and the first data-center custom-silicon shipments. FY28-29 raised to +4.5%/+6% (were +3%/+5%): the hyperscaler custom-silicon agreements are now signed, with binding purchase commitments large enough to vest 4M of the 25M Amazon warrant shares, so data center is a contracted revenue line rather than a target. FY30 onward unchanged, fading to 3% against a 6.2% through-cycle 10y CAGR.
base.margin_rationale: Years 1-3 cut (were 33/34/35%): FY26 came in at 31.9% and exited at ~26-29% in H2 on higher wafer, packaging and memory costs and R&D up $1.2B; management expects supplier costs to keep hurting margins, with its own price increases fully in gross margin only from H2 FY27. Recovery to the unchanged 36% mature level is pushed out a year -- still below the FY24-25 37-38% because Apple flagship-modem mix leaves and custom silicon carries lower gross margin. QTL held its 72% EBT margin.
base.sbc_rationale: Years 1-3 raised (were 10.3/10.1/9.9%): FY26 actual 10.6%, and the equity-for-cash-bonus award runs through FY27, plus $342M of Modular retention stock expensed over four years. Path rejoins the prior glide from year 4.
base.tax_rationale: Years 1-3 lowered (were 17/18/19%): FY26 cash tax was $1,644M including the final $663M repatriation instalment, i.e. ~$980M underlying (~11% of operating income) with domestic R&D now expensed as incurred; the CAMT exposure is gone (Notice 2026-07) and $5.8B of deferred tax assets remain to be used. Ramps back to the unchanged normal 19% by year 4 -- the shelter is not perpetuated.
base.capex_rationale: Raised across the path (was 4.0% fading to 3.2%): FY26 capex doubled to $2,494M (5.8% of revenue) and management expects it to increase further in the near term for engineering infrastructure and IC test. Peaks at 6.3% in FY27, fades to 3.5% (was 3.2%) as the data-center build completes; D&A follows with a lag (FY26 3.8%, incl. Alphawave/Modular intangibles) and settles at 3.4%.
base.wc_rationale: Fabless chip seller: receivables + inventory exceed payables, so growth consumes cash (negative capture on the revenue change). The FY26 $2.1B inventory build is not assumed to reverse.

bull.rationale: Growth path unchanged. Margin years 1-2 cut (were 33.5/35%) for the same FY26 exit rate and supplier-cost evidence as base; SBC years 1-3, capex, D&A and cash-tax years 1-3 re-anchored to FY26 actuals as in base.

bear.rationale: Growth path unchanged. Margin years 1-4 cut (were 31/31/31.5/32%): the H2 FY26 exit rate (~26-29%) is already below the prior bear year 1, so the trough is set at 28% and the 32% mature level is reached a year later. SBC years 1-2, capex, D&A and cash-tax years 1-3 re-anchored to FY26 actuals as in base.

scenario_narratives.base: Handset revenue (FY26 $24.1B, -13%) keeps falling in FY27 as memory-supply constraints and price increases cut Android OEM builds and Apple's in-house modem finishes displacing Qualcomm across the iPhone line; Android flagship share holds against MediaTek. Automotive (FY26 $6.0B, +52%) and IoT keep compounding, and the data-center business moves from Alphawave IP revenue to shipments under signed hyperscaler custom-silicon agreements from Q1 FY27 -- enough to hold FY27 revenue flat and return it to mid-single-digit growth in FY28-29, though far short of management's $5B/$15B targets. QTL royalties stay stable at ~$5.5B on a 72% margin. Margins trough in FY27 (supplier cost inflation, a $10B+ R&D base, elevated capex) and recover as price increases land from H2 FY27, settling below the FY24-25 level on mix.
scenario_narratives.bull: Data center AI becomes a real third leg: the Amazon agreement (warrant milestones run to $60B of purchases over ten years) ramps on schedule and a second hyperscaler follows, taking data-center revenue into the mid-single-digit billions by FY29; Alphawave connectivity IP and Modular's software stack attach to custom silicon; Oryon CPUs win share in Windows PCs. Memory supply normalises during FY27, releasing a deferred on-device-AI handset upgrade cycle, automotive runs past $8B, and operating leverage on the now-built opex base lifts adj EBITDA margin back above 38%. Revenue compounds high-single-digit for three years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The memory-driven handset downturn already visible in H2 FY26 deepens and persists through FY28, on top of the Apple loss and MediaTek/in-house Chinese silicon gains; supplier cost inflation cannot be passed on, so QCT gross margin does not recover. Custom-silicon shipments ramp slowly and at thin margins against Broadcom, Marvell and hyperscaler in-house teams, leaving a $10B R&D base, two stock-funded acquisitions and a doubled capex budget under-earning. A renewed antitrust or licensee challenge to 'no license, no chips' trims QTL rates. Revenue falls ~9% over two years and recovers only at GDP-like rates; margins trough at 28% and never regain the FY26 level by much.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged at 25/50/25 by decision. Bear stays at 25% (house default 15%): the hyperscaler custom-silicon agreements make the data-center pivot less unproven, but the memory-led handset downturn that the bear case describes has started and FY26 margins exited below the prior bear year 1 -- the two roughly offset. Base 50%: auto/IoT growth and the contracted data-center ramp are visible in the filing. Bull stays at 25% (default 35%): it still needs data center, PC share and a handset upgrade cycle to all go right. A second hyperscaler programme or a visible gross-margin recovery in H2 FY27 would move weight from bear to bull; Q1-Q2 FY27 handset revenue below ~$5B a quarter would move it the other way.

valuation_philosophy.summary: QCOM is valued as a cyclical fabless semiconductor plus a stable licensing annuity on a strict owner-FCF basis: SBC and the cash taxes paid on net-share settlement (10.6% of revenue combined in FY26) are charged in the flows and the share count held flat. FY26 was a trough for cash conversion (owner FCF 9.4% of revenue vs 20.1% in FY25) and the trough is not carried forward, but neither is the recovery assumed to be quick: margins bottom in FY27 and capex stays elevated for three years. The terminal value is capped at a cyclical 14x (16x bull, 12x bear). The data-center business is now a contracted revenue line in base, with the large-scale outcome reserved for the bull case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Memory-supply constraints and device price increases cut handset OEM demand for longer than the 'next several quarters' management flags
Supplier cost inflation (wafer, packaging, test) is not recovered by the price increases planned for H2 FY27
Apple modem attrition faster or deeper than base; two customers were 22% and 20% of FY26 revenue
Custom-silicon data-center revenue ramps slower or at lower margin than assumed; the Amazon warrant (25M shares at $161.26) is a contra-revenue cost and 2.3% potential dilution if exercised
Antitrust/licensee challenge to the QTL royalty model
SBC + withholding treatment: the street basis (SBC as non-cash) values QCOM materially higher; the house figure depends on charging ~$4.6B/yr of equity comp, and SBC rose 24% in FY26
Acquisitions paid in stock (Alphawave 11M shares, Modular 18M) -- further stock-funded deals would dilute a count the model holds flat
Discount rate: the 10-year Treasury above 5% costs ~11% of value versus the prior build; a move back toward 4.3% would restore it
Cash tax: R&D expensing and the $5.8B deferred tax asset could keep cash tax below 19% for longer than the three-year ramp (upside)

Each bridge step is a full rebuild with that driver group swapped in, in the order listed, so the steps sum exactly; the split between steps depends on that order.
